subtitulo: The same summary for two audiences
descripcion: At C2 a summary is calibrated to what the specific audience already knows, compressing shared background aggressively while expanding exactly the part that's genuinely new to them — the same source material summarised differently for two different audiences.

filas: why it matters, in plain terms
a short bridge naming both readings

ejemplos.texto: Skipping the methodology, which you'll know already, the one real surprise was the effect size.
In plain terms, this means prices are likely to rise faster than expected.
For those new to this, here's the one thing that actually matters.

notas: Naming what you're skipping (skipping the methodology, which you'll know already) signals respect for an expert audience's time.
The same source can be summarised in two genuinely different ways depending on the audience, not just simplified once for everyone.
For a general audience, expanding why it matters in plain terms is more valuable than expanding technical detail they didn't ask for.

es.en: Spanish has the same tools for acknowledging shared knowledge («como ya sabéis» – as you know), so audience-based summarising is not new. The English addition is to leave whole known parts out, signalled with phrases like I won't go over… again.
es.es: El español tiene las mismas herramientas para reconocer conocimientos compartidos («como ya sabéis» – «as you know»), por lo que resumir según la audiencia no es nuevo. El añadido inglés es omitir por completo partes ya conocidas, señalándolo con expresiones como «I won't go over… again».

de.en: German has «wie Sie wissen» and the compact «bekanntlich» (as is well known), so acknowledging shared knowledge is familiar. English leaves known parts out with phrases like I won't go over… again, where German speakers tend to summarise everything.
de.de: Deutsch hat «wie Sie wissen» und das kompakte «bekanntlich» («as is well known»), daher ist das Markieren gemeinsamen Wissens vertraut. Englisch lässt Bekanntes häufig mit Formeln wie «I won't go over… again» weg, während Deutschsprachige dazu neigen, alles noch einmal zusammenzufassen.

it.en: «Come sapete» corresponds to as you know, and «non sto a ripetere» to I won't go over… again. Audience-based summarising therefore transfers directly.
it.it: «Come sapete» corrisponde a «as you know», e «non sto a ripetere» a «I won't go over… again». Il riassunto adattato al pubblico si trasferisce quindi direttamente.

fr.en: «Comme vous le savez» corresponds to as you know, and «je ne reviens pas sur…» to I won't go back over…. Audience-based summarising therefore transfers directly.
fr.fr: «Comme vous le savez» correspond à «as you know», et «je ne reviens pas sur…» à «I won't go back over…». Le résumé adapté à l'audience se transfère donc directement.

pt.en: «Como sabem» corresponds to as you know, and «não vou repetir» to I won't go over… again. Audience-based summarising therefore transfers directly.
pt.pt: «Como sabem» corresponde a «as you know», e «não vou repetir» a «I won't go over… again». O resumo adaptado ao público se transfere diretamente.

errores: Giving the same summary regardless of audience, wasting an expert's time or losing a general reader.
Compressing the one part that's actually new to this audience.
Expanding technical detail for an audience that needs the implications instead.

es: «*A grandes rasgos*» rendered as *At big traits* instead of *Broadly speaking*.
de: «*Im Grossen und Ganzen*» rendered as *In the big and whole* instead of *By and large*.
it: «*A grandi linee*» rendered as *At big lines* instead of *Broadly speaking*.
fr: «*Dans les grandes lignes*» rendered as *In the big lines* instead of *Broadly speaking*.
pt: «*Em linhas gerais*» rendered as *In general lines* instead of *Broadly speaking*.

mision.consigna: Summarise the state of an ageing system twice: for the engineers who maintain it and for the manager who funds it.
requisitos: shared background compressed aggressively for the experts
the genuinely new part expanded for each audience
one *I'll assume you know…, so let's focus on…*
use *technical debt*, *a single point of failure* and *to future-proof*

microtareas.texto: List what the engineers already know about *a legacy system*. Cut it.
Write what the manager needs that the engineers don't.
Record 2 minutes on *interoperability* for someone new to it.

autochequeo: Is the summary calibrated to what this specific audience already knows?
Is shared background compressed, not repeated at length?
Is the genuinely new or significant part expanded, not buried?
Would an expert feel their time was respected?
Would a general reader understand why it matters?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on whether the summary is calibrated to the intended audience's existing knowledge. Check what's compressed versus expanded. Do not rewrite the text.
